walkthroughs.body_html:
Applied Psychology Options (Child / Criminal / Environmental / Sport and Exercise) — a core area of A-Level Psychology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Applied Psychology Options (Child / Criminal / Environmental / Sport and Exercise) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Applied Psychology Options (Child / Criminal / Environmental / Sport and Exercise).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: Canter
FBI
Lombroso
Eysenck

options: Sutherland
Eysenck
Bandura
Lombroso

mcqs.q: Why does the cognitive approach use INFERENCE?
options: Because brain scans are unreliable.
Reliability is for quantitative, validity for qualitative.
Because cognitive psychologists guess instead of measuring.
Mental processes cannot be directly observed, so they are inferred from behaviour.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between reliability and validity?
options: Because brain scans are unreliable.
They are essentially the same thing.
Reliability is consistency; validity is whether it measures what it claims to.
Reliability is for quantitative, validity for qualitative.

mcqs.q: When is deception in research ever acceptable?
options: Reliability is for quantitative, validity for qualitative.
Never - deception is always banned.
Always - psychologists can deceive freely.
When demand characteristics would otherwise invalidate the study, with thorough debrief and ethics approval.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Eysenck's theory”?
options: Sutherland (1939): criminal behaviour learned from associates whose pro-crime attitudes outweigh anti-crime ones.
Lombroso's (1876) outdated theory that criminals are evolutionary throwbacks identifiable by physical features.
Criminals score high on extraversion, neuroticism and psychoticism (E, N, P); inherited nervous system underactivity.
Canter's UK approach: statistical analysis of crime scene data to derive profiles; investigative psychology.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Atavistic form”?
options: Imprisonment aims to deter, rehabilitate, incapacitate and protect; UK recidivism around 48% within one year.
Sutherland (1939): criminal behaviour learned from associates whose pro-crime attitudes outweigh anti-crime ones.
Lombroso's (1876) outdated theory that criminals are evolutionary throwbacks identifiable by physical features.
FBI approach (Ressler 1986): classify crime scene as organised or disorganised to infer offender characteristics.
